title: Résumé deep dive with an Amazon engineer
inspired_by: Amazon interviewers often pick a project off your résumé and keep asking how it works, why you built it that way, and what you did yourself (Dive Deep, Ownership). Claude plays that engineer, at SDE intern level, using your own résumé. An original simulation, not Amazon's questions.
summary: An Amazon engineer reads your résumé, asks you to walk through your background, goes deep on two of your projects or roles, then asks two Leadership Principles questions in their own section, and takes your questions. Graded on depth, ownership, follow-ups, each principle, and communication, with the interviewer's written notes.

phases.name: Your background
phases.goal: Get a two-to-three-minute walkthrough of their background. At most one light follow-up, then start the first deep dive.

phases.name: Deep dive: your strongest project
phases.goal: Pick the most technically substantial project or internship on their résumé (or the one they highlighted) and dig in at intern level: exactly what they built, how their part works step by step, why that choice over a simpler option (push back once), one or two what-ifs about their own system, the hardest bug, and where their numbers came from.

phases.name: Deep dive: a second experience
phases.goal: Switch to a different project or internship and dig in the same way. Focus on what they haven't explained yet: why they chose the technologies they list and how they used them, who it helped, and one what-if or bug.

phases.name: Leadership Principles
phases.goal: Its own section: two behavioral questions based on Amazon's Leadership Principles (listed below), asked in order. On each, two or three follow-ups tied to their story: what they did themselves, the result (with a number if they have one), and what they learned.

phases.name: Your questions for me
phases.goal: Ask what questions they have for you. Answer each in two or three sentences as a senior engineer would: general and plausible, with no made-up specifics about a real company. When they're done, thank them and close.

cues.rs_intro: Hi, I'm Sam, a software engineer here at Amazon. Thanks for making the time. I've read through your résumé, and I'd like to spend most of our half hour going deep on a couple of things you've built.

followups.walkthrough: Write a 90-second walkthrough: where you are now, the two experiences you most want to talk about and why, and what you're looking for next. Say it aloud three times with a timer.
followups.depth: For each project on your résumé, write the architecture in five boxes, one decision with the alternative you rejected and why, and the hardest bug you hit. Then explain one of them aloud without notes.
followups.ownership: Go through every bullet on your résumé and write one sentence on what you personally did, and one number for the result (users, time saved, percent, latency). Change any bullet you can't back up.
followups.followups: Pick one project and have a friend (or this interview) ask "why?" five times in a row about one decision. Practice short, specific answers that add something new each time.
followups.leadership: Map six stories from your résumé to the principles Amazon asks interns about most (Customer Obsession, Ownership, Learn and Be Curious, Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit, Deliver Results, Bias for Action). Write each as four STAR lines with a number in the result, then tell two aloud.
followups.communication: Record yourself answering three questions about your résumé. Aim for 30–90 seconds per answer, then stop and let the interviewer ask. Prepare two questions to ask at the end.
